frequency_question: What proportion of major Treasury debt intervention programs that are initiated successfully reach their designated operational volume scaling targets without being prematurely curtailed, capped, or suspended before the target deadline?
membership_rule: Includes major structural Treasury/Fed operations (e.g., Operation Twist, large-scale asset purchase programs, Treasury buyback implementation phases) that had explicit volume scale-up milestones. Excludes one-off emergency liquidity facilities with entirely reactive, ad-hoc sizing.

cases.name: Fed Large-Scale Asset Purchase (QE3 open-ended scaling)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major structured debt management expansion cycles named; all achieved their scaling objectives.
known_gaps: Sample is restricted to major post-1990 U.S. federal debt management structural operations.
skeleton: Named historical debt management scaling initiatives categorized by whether announced expansion pathways were fully executed to their target scale or curtailed early.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 historical comparable structural debt management scaling plans successfully reaching announced operational volume milestones.
validity_reason: Treasury debt management operating procedures and scaling norms evolve slowly across decades.
